prompt_en: A complex water photograph centered on a person whose face and short hair follow the attached reference, at a reed-fringed river landing where water is visibly present. She wears an ecru linen shirt with an open collar and rolled sleeves, charcoal trousers and flat shoes. Preserve the visible facial proportions, dark eyes, softly rounded chin, natural full lips, short dark bob and wispy fringe of the photograph; her clothing and the surrounding circumstances are authored for this scene. A modest river ferry has just passed farther out, its stern facing us: it is the one moving hull or object producing the disturbance. Its V-shaped wake ridges joined behind it stay visibly attached to the stern and widen toward the landing. Between those ridges, a trailing disturbed surface distinct from ambient waves forms a narrow churned lane; the adjacent river is smoother. Repeated low crests curve through the reed stems toward a weathered stone step. A small blue wooden skiff floats a short rope-length from the landing, its bow momentarily raised by the arriving crest, a clear strip of moving water separating the hull from the stones. The skiff's curved blue side is an object meeting the liquid surface as the arriving crest reaches its chine. This hull contact throws a raised liquid sheet at that contact into a curved translucent fan just outside the blue planks. Small detached drops beyond the sheet separate visibly from its breaking rim and catch the same afternoon light. Standing on the upper dry step with her feet apart, she leans slightly back with softly bent elbows and both hands close together around the taut bow line. The line is visible from her hands to the iron ring at the skiff's bow; she is taking up the sudden slack to keep the boat within reach. Her gaze follows that rising bow. A slight brow crease and softly parted lips convey the concentration of this brief interruption; warm reflected light and wind-shifted strands keep her presence quietly intimate. At the foreground step, the same crest spreads into a shallow translucent sheet, flicking separate droplets upward from the stone edge. The sheet thins into narrow rivulets through the joints and returns to the river below; their wet paths shine against the drier upper stones. A faint ochre sediment stripe runs continuously across the upright stone riser at an older high-water level, distinct above the fresh dark wet film. One tall reed stem on the right bank is the one visible reflected object. Its inverted or rippled surface image sits immediately beneath that same stem and bends across the crests. The stem's base at the bank establishes geometric continuity between object and water plane; the calmer water beside the wake retains the longer reflection of the same stem. Frame this as an observed environmental portrait from a nearby upper landing, showing her face, both hands, supporting feet, the rope connection and the water's impact edge together. Let the person and lifted bow read first, then the spreading water and the distant ferry explain the disturbance. Afternoon sun from camera-left picks out tiny silver flecks across the wave faces tilted toward it; the intervening troughs stay dark green-brown, and the droplets and her face share that same illumination. Use a horizontal environmental portrait with enough depth of field for the action, wake source and shoreline traces to remain clear; retain believable skin texture and the river's muted green-brown color.
